proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived and independently reviewed a matched homogeneous-benchmark honest-length family n^(-4 beta/(9+4 beta)) for rational 0<beta<=9/22, generalized complex Fourier-modulus channels, a total finite main-record interval, and categorical converses. Math review passed after two lawful citation attestations and a direct proof of the exact closed-subset contraction lemma, but the novelty assessment remained incremental with paper-score ceiling 6.2 below the field threshold 7.4. The independent validity gate found no bounded in-scope repair: extending precision beyond exact homogeneity or supplying informative finite-sample construction requires new research; formalization was not entered.
tldr: The unnormalized pair Gini measures dispersion of conditional mean treatment benefits. For each fixed public rational \(0<\beta\le9/22\), full-class finite-sample honesty has matched homogeneous-benchmark expected length \(n^{-4\beta/(9+4\beta)}\), with no logarithmic loss. The order is the same without calibration, with any calibration budget, or with the channel revealed. One total finite procedure uses only the original main records and covers every homogeneous constant-arm pair while remaining honest against rough confounding throughout the Fourier-modulus class. The specialization \(\beta=1/10\) gives exponent \(2/47\); the elbow \(\beta=9/22\) gives \(2/13\). The supporting full-class worst-length floor is \(c_{\ast}\max\{n^{-4\beta/(9+4\beta)},(1+m)^{-\beta/2}\}\). Its necessary lower-bound calibration crossover is \(1+m\asymp n^{8/(9+4\beta)}\), or \(n^{40/47}\) at \(\beta=1/10\). A matched global frontier and a sufficient or exact oracle calibration budget remain unresolved.
